courses.title: Speech and Hearing Sciences
courses.outline: The aim of this course is an understanding of the nature of sound, how sound is perceived by humans and how speech is produced. Content also includes the dimensions and parameters of sound; transmission of sound; analysis of sound; resonance; measurement of sound; range of hearing; the concept of threshold; concepts of loudness and pitch; masking as well as binaural hearing; speech production; nature of speech; vocal anatomy, the vocal tract articulators and resonators; linguistic function of speech sounds; as well as spectra and spectrograms.

Included in the syllabus is also aspects of endocrinology and nutrition and diet. It is a full course of lectures, interactive weekly tutorials, practicals and demonstrations. Special emphasis is placed on neuro-anatomy and neurophysiology.

courses.outline: The integrated courses HUB2017H, PTY2000S and PTY3009F extend across MBChB years two and three and provide the student with a detailed understanding of the normal structure and function of the human body and how these are affected when the body suffers from disease. Advanced topics include stem cells, their biology and application, cancer biology, and infectious agents, infectious diseases and inherited diseases.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology Part 1
courses.outline: This course introduces students to selected areas of psychological inquiry, offering an overview of the field's foundational and applied dimensions. These areas can range widely, from, for example, the history of the discipline, to biological and cognitive processes, to mental health. In addition to engaging with key conceptual and empirical debates, students will begin cultivating essential academic skills, with particular attention to ethical scholarship, academic writing, and the conventions of psychological communication. courses.title: Introduction to Psychology Part 2
courses.outline: This course builds on the content covered in Introduction to Psychology Part 1. There is emphasis on research methods, both quantitative and qualitative methods. This course deepens students’ engagement with psychology as a scientific and interpretive discipline concerned with understanding behaviour, thought, and emotion in context. Emphasis is placed on developing a critical appreciation of different psychological inquiry and analysis approaches. Through exposure to a range of thematic areas, students build competencies in research literacy, academic writing, and the evaluation of evidence.

Some of the major topics covered will include race and racism, social identity and social change, intergroup contact, and social influence.

courses.title: Beginners' Xhosa for Mbchb
courses.outline: An introduction to the noun class system of Xhosa and how this generates the concords used in creating sentences. A simple explanation of Xhosa moods: indicative (making a statement), subjunctive (giving advice and making suggestions), participial (used in a wide range of contexts).
